title: Carthage founded
description: Phoenicians from Tyre, led in legend by Queen Dido, found the city that comes to dominate the trade of the western Mediterranean.

title: Battle of the Bagradas River
description: A Carthaginian army led by the Spartan Xanthippus destroys the Roman army of Regulus, ending Rome's invasion of Africa in the First Punic War.

title: Battle of Zama
description: Scipio defeats Hannibal and ends the Second Punic War, leaving Rome the leading power of the western Mediterranean.

title: Battle of Thapsus
description: Julius Caesar defeats the republican army of Metellus Scipio and King Juba of Numidia, and turns Numidia into a Roman province.

title: Carthage refounded as a Roman colony
description: Julius Caesar orders a new city on the ruins, and under Augustus it becomes the capital of Roman Africa and one of the largest cities of the empire.

title: Vandals take Carthage
description: Gaiseric seizes the city and Rome's richest grain province, and makes it the capital of a kingdom whose fleet sacks Rome in 455.

title: Battle of Ad Decimum
description: Belisarius defeats King Gelimer and enters Carthage, returning Africa to the eastern Roman Empire.

title: Battle of Sufetula
description: An Arab army from Egypt defeats and kills the exarch Gregory, the first step in the Muslim conquest of the Maghreb.

title: Kairouan founded
description: Uqba ibn Nafi founds a garrison town and mosque that become the base for the conquest of the Maghreb and its first centre of Islamic learning.

title: Arabs take Carthage
description: Hassan ibn al-Nu'man captures and demolishes the last Byzantine stronghold in Africa, and Tunis grows up in its place.

title: Aghlabid emirate founded
description: The caliph Harun al-Rashid grants Ifriqiya to Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab, whose dynasty rules it as its own and conquers Sicily.

title: Fatimids overthrow the Aghlabids
description: Kutama Berbers led by an Ismaili missionary take the Aghlabid capital, and their imam is proclaimed caliph of the Shia dynasty that later conquers Egypt.

title: Banu Hilal sack Kairouan
description: Arab tribes sent west from Egypt ruin the Zirid capital, and the Arabic language and herding spread through the countryside.

title: Hafsids become independent
description: The governor Abu Zakariya Yahya breaks with the Almohads and founds a dynasty that makes Tunis the capital for three and a half centuries.

title: Louis IX dies at Tunis
description: The French king dies of disease in his camp while attacking Tunis, and the Eighth Crusade is abandoned.

title: Birth of Ibn Khaldun
description: The historian is born in Tunis; his Muqaddimah sets out a theory of how states and societies rise and fall.

title: Charles V takes Tunis
description: The emperor drives out Hayreddin Barbarossa and restores the Hafsid ruler under Spanish protection.

title: Ottoman conquest of Tunis
description: An Ottoman fleet and army take Tunis and its harbour fortress from Spain for good, and Tunisia becomes an Ottoman province.

title: Husainid dynasty founded
description: The cavalry commander Husayn ibn Ali is made bey, and his family reigns until 1957.

title: Slavery abolished
description: Ahmad Bey frees all slaves in the country, earlier than any other Muslim state.

title: Constitution of 1861
description: Muhammad III as-Sadiq brings into force the first written constitution in the Arab world, which is suspended three years later.

title: Treaty of Bardo
description: With French troops outside his palace, the bey signs a treaty that makes Tunisia a French protectorate.

title: Neo Destour founded
description: Habib Bourguiba and other young nationalists break from the Destour to form the party that leads Tunisia to independence.

title: Axis surrender in Tunisia
description: The last German and Italian forces in Africa surrender, and more than 230,000 men are taken prisoner.

title: Independence
description: France recognises the independence of Tunisia, and Habib Bourguiba becomes prime minister and, the next year, president.

title: Code of Personal Status
description: A new family law bans polygamy and requires a court for divorce and the consent of both parties for marriage.

title: Israeli raid on the PLO headquarters
description: Israeli aircraft bomb the headquarters that the Palestine Liberation Organization had moved to Tunisia in 1982.

title: Ben Ali removes Bourguiba
description: The prime minister Zine El Abidine Ben Ali has the ageing president declared unfit and takes his place, ruling for 23 years.

title: Mohamed Bouazizi sets himself on fire
description: A street vendor's protest against harassment by officials sets off demonstrations that spread across Tunisia and then the Arab world.

title: Ben Ali flees
description: After four weeks of protests the president leaves for Saudi Arabia, the first ruler to fall in the Arab Spring.

title: New constitution adopted
description: The constituent assembly passes a constitution agreed between Islamists and secular parties.

title: Sousse attack
description: A gunman kills 38 people, most of them British tourists, at a beach hotel.
